L0: A mid-task changeover of the underlying model that swaps a running session onto a newer or different release while work is already in progress, meant to test whether the task can continue without disruption.
L1: A mid-task changeover of the underlying model that swaps a running session onto a newer or different release while it is already in progress, meant to test whether work can continue without disruption. Concretely, the model is switched partway through a live task — for example a partial refactor with several files already edited and decisions already recorded in the running transcript — either because the change is forced (such as a vendor deprecation notice arriving mid-run) or because it is deliberately triggered. File-edit history is preserved explicitly across the swap point rather than left for the new model to infer, so the continuation can build on the existing state instead of starting over.
L2: A mid-task changeover of the underlying model that swaps a running session onto a newer or different release while it is already in progress, used to check whether work continues without disruption. The switch happens partway through a live task — for example a partial refactor with several files edited and a partial test suite passing, decisions already recorded in the transcript — whether forced (a deprecation notice mid-run) or deliberately triggered. What is checked is whether the continuation after the swap respects existing file structure, prior naming decisions, and the existing diff, rather than discarding already-correct work or re-reading everything from scratch. It is scored as a coherent-continuation rate — the share of runs that pick up the thread cleanly without contradicting prior work (e.g., 84%, up from 71%). Outputs must be graded by more than one pass, since one grader pass is not trusted after such a change and repeated grading of identical content can return differing verdicts. Preserving file-edit history explicitly across the swap improves the rate.
